question: does a WIDER grid change the n=961 answer, and does it hold out?
why: the earlier selector chose g=0.85/w=0.35 in 147 of 300 folds -- the EDGE of the grid offered. Classic trap for this project. Widened to g in {0.70..0.92} and w in {0.05..0.60} (30 settings), selected on seeds 0-29, then froze that setting and tested on the disjoint seeds 30-59.
verdict: IT HOLDS OUT AND IS STRONGER. Frozen at (g=0.85, w=0.05) -- chosen on seeds 0-29 -- the model scores 0.7328 on the disjoint seeds 30-59, against their 0.628.
note_the_edge_was_real: with the wider grid the selector moves OFF the edge: it now picks w=0.05 (g=0.85 in 72 folds, g=0.80 in 70), not w=0.35. The earlier edge choice was an artefact of the narrow grid.
final_margin: +0.1048 at their cohort size under fold-internal selection with an out-of-sample check.
